title: Marco-o1: Towards Open Reasoning Models for Open-Ended Solutions
data_curation: Marco-o1 builds three SFT datasets totaling 60,266 samples. The Open-O1 CoT Dataset (Filtered), 45,125 samples, is derived from the open-source Open-O1 project's CoT data by applying heuristic and quality-filtering processes so the model adopts structured reasoning patterns. The Marco-o1 CoT Dataset (Synthetic), 10,000 samples, is generated using MCTS to construct complex reasoning pathways. The Marco Instruction Dataset, 5,141 samples, adds instruction-following data to preserve general task competence. All three are combined for full-parameter supervised fine-tuning of Qwen2-7B-Instruct. No explicit de-duplication or scaling-law study is described; the emphasis is on mixing CoT reasoning traces with instruction data rather than large-scale data curation, and the synthetic CoT portion is produced by the same MCTS machinery later used at inference.
curriculum: Training is essentially a single SFT stage: full-parameter fine-tuning of Qwen2-7B-Instruct on the combined CoT + instruction data produces Marco-o1-CoT. There is no separate preference-optimization, RL, or distillation stage; MCTS, action-granularity variants, and the reflection prompt are applied at inference time on top of the SFT model rather than as training curricula. The synthetic CoT data is itself generated via MCTS, creating a loose generate-then-train loop, but no multi-stage RL or self-play schedule is described. Future work proposes adding Outcome/Process Reward Modeling and RL to fine-tune decision-making, indicating the current pipeline is a flat SFT-then-search arrangement.
method: The core contribution couples CoT fine-tuning with inference-time MCTS and a reasoning-action strategy. In the MCTS framework each node is a reasoning state and actions are LLM-generated steps or mini-steps; rollouts continue to a terminal state and are scored by a confidence-based reward. For each generated token the confidence c_i is the softmax of its log-probability against the top-5 alternative tokens' log-probabilities; the rollout reward v is the average c_i over all tokens, used to select promising search paths. Action granularity is varied—full step, 64-token mini-step, or 32-token mini-step—to trade search breadth against resolution. A reflection mechanism appends 'Wait! Maybe I made some mistakes! I need to rethink from scratch.' to trigger self-critique and re-reasoning, fixing roughly half of initially-incorrect hard problems. The work targets open-ended tasks where rewards are hard to quantify, using model confidence in lieu of an external reward model.
eval_metrics: Evaluation uses the MGSM multilingual grade-school math benchmark (English and Chinese subsets) with accuracy and Test@N (Test@1, Test@8, Test@32, the fraction solved correctly at least once in N guesses). A qualitative case study compares slang/colloquial translation against Google Translate. On MGSM-En, Marco-o1-MCTS (step) reaches 90.40% Test@1 (vs 84.00% Qwen2-7B-Instruct), with the paper reporting +6.17% improvement; on MGSM-Zh, Marco-o1-MCTS (mini-step of 32) reaches 82.40% (vs 76.80% baseline), +5.60%. Test@32 climbs to 99.60% (En) and 96.80% (Zh). Notably, Marco-o1-CoT alone underperforms the base model on MGSM-Zh (71.20% vs 76.80%), attributed to English-only CoT training data. No standard coding or agentic benchmarks are reported.
key_results: Marco-o1-MCTS (step): 90.40% on MGSM-En vs 84.00% Qwen2-7B-Instruct (+6.17%). Marco-o1-MCTS (mini-step 32): 82.40% on MGSM-Zh vs 76.80% (+5.60%). Test@32 reaches 99.60% (En) / 96.80% (Zh).
evolution_note: Marco-o1 is an early open attempt (Nov 2024) to demystify OpenAI o1's reasoning by combining CoT SFT with AlphaZero-style MCTS and self-reflection, explicitly extending the reasoning-model trend to open-ended and multilingual/translation tasks. It motivates later work on learned reward models (ORM/PRM) and RL-based decision fine-tuning to replace its noisy confidence-score reward.
